description: Autonomous orchestrator recycle CORE: cycle-close arms a dedicated marker, a wrapper-owned watcher SIGTERMs the orchestrator claude, and the fresh respawn rehydrates via an explicit signal (CAM-141 fix), removing the manual /exit.

officialDocsConsulted.summary: Confirms hooks CANNOT terminate an interactive session: Stop/SubagentStop can only force continuation (exit 2 / continue:false), and no hook can initiate session termination. Sessions end via /exit, Ctrl-C, or an external signal (SIGTERM). Validates the CAM-162 decision that the wrapper (not a hook, not the sidecar) owns termination via SIGTERM on the PID.

Documents --session-id, --model, and --permission-mode (all already used by the orchestrator pane command). No in-session self-exit primitive is documented; interactive sessions are terminated externally, confirming SIGTERM-on-PID as the deterministic recycle mechanism.

userStories.title: Review round 2 fix 002: address reviewer finding
userStories.notes: WARNING [.gitignore]: Two new runtime files written under .claude/ are not gitignored in either tree, unlike their sidecar analogues (.cam-sidecar.pid and cam-supervisor.log both ARE gitignored): (1) .claude/.cam-watcher.pid (WATCHER_PID_FILE, written by writeWatcherPid in run.ts, US-R1-001) and (2) .claude/cam-recycle-watcher.log (opened by spawnWatcherDefault in run.ts, US-004). The pid file lingers after a normal detach until cam stop removes it, and the log is never removed, so both appear as untracked runtime state in the dogfood repo and in every downstream project (templates/.gitignore is what cam init installs). Fix: add .claude/.cam-watcher.pid and .claude/cam-recycle-watcher.log to both .gitignore and templates/.gitignore, then re-run bun run embed-vendor (templates/.gitignore is embedded in src/vendor/_generated.ts) and verify embed-vendor:check is clean.

userStories.title: Review round 1 fix 001: address reviewer finding
userStories.notes: WARNING [src/commands/run.ts:679]: The recycle watcher is orphaned by `cam stop`. The watcher is spawned identically to the sidecar (Bun.spawn, not detached, no proc.unref()) and survives `cam run`'s normal exit because main() ends in process.exit() after the blocking tmux attach returns on detach. But unlike the sidecar, its pid is never persisted (no writeSidecarPid equivalent) and performStop's fallback scoped scan only matches argv[1]==='sidecar' (stop.ts:214, matchesSidecarForProject). So after the normal detach -> `cam stop` teardown, the watcher keeps polling .claude/.cam-orch-recycle every 2s forever, and one leaks per run/stop cycle. US-004 AC1 (kill in the SIGINT/SIGTERM cleanup handler) is met, but the PRD note's recommendation to persist the pid "so it is killable" was not followed, so the documented kill-switch does not reach it. Fix: persist the watcher pid and kill it in performStop (mirror writeSidecarPid + the sidecar kill path), or extend the fallback scan to match `cam orch-recycle-watch`.

userStories.title: Recycle watcher module and cam orch-recycle-watch command
userStories.description: As the wrapper, I need a watcher that detects the recycle marker, resolves the orchestrator claude PID without a new tmux surface, sends a graceful SIGTERM, and consumes the marker once, so termination is deterministic and does not re-fire on the respawn.
acceptanceCriteria: A new module src/commands/orch-recycle-watch.ts implements a poll loop that detects the recycle marker (ORCH_RECYCLE_MARKER), and on presence resolves the orchestrator claude PID, sends SIGTERM, then removes the marker. [oracle: grep -rq 'ORCH_RECYCLE_MARKER' src/commands/orch-recycle-watch.ts]

The watcher fires SIGTERM on the presence of the MARKER, never on the handoff file; a unit test with injected deps proves SIGTERM is sent when the marker is present and NOT sent when only a handoff (no marker) is present. [oracle: bun test test/commands/orch-recycle-watch.test.ts]
The kill signal is a graceful SIGTERM (signal 15), not SIGKILL, so claude can exit cleanly; a unit test asserts the signal value. [oracle: bun test test/commands/orch-recycle-watch.test.ts]

Consume-once: after firing SIGTERM the watcher removes the marker so a single arm triggers at most one SIGTERM (it does not re-kill the respawned session); a unit test asserts exactly one kill per marker arm. [oracle: bun test test/commands/orch-recycle-watch.test.ts]

The PID is resolved WITHOUT opening a new tmux surface: the watcher reads the current orchestrator session-id fresh each poll from ORCH_SESSION_MARKER (.cam-orch-session) and scopes PID resolution to it (e.g. pgrep -f on the session-id). [oracle: grep -q 'ORCH_SESSION_MARKER' src/commands/orch-recycle-watch.ts]
The watcher does not call tmux (keeps the no-new-tmux-surface invariant). [oracle: reviewer-judgment]

`cam orch-recycle-watch` is registered as an INTERNAL subcommand in index.ts (not listed in top-level HELP), invokable via Bun.spawn like `cam sidecar`. [oracle: grep -q "case 'orch-recycle-watch'" index.ts]

Header comment claims 'Responds to --help when invoked directly', but the index.ts case only calls runOrchRecycleWatch() and returns, and runOrchRecycleWatch parses no args, so `cam orch-recycle-watch --help` starts the poll loop instead of printing help. Comment-vs-runtime mismatch (open from review round 1). Drop the claim or add a --help guard.
Stale `// eslint-disable-next-line no-constant-condition` on the `while (true)` loop. The project lints with biome, not eslint, so the directive is inert cruft (open from review round 1).

makeResolvePidFn selects the child claude PID by taking the LAST pgrep line (assumed highest PID). Relies on pgrep ascending-PID order and no PID wraparound; documented and proven by the e2e test, but fragile. Consider `pgrep -n` or matching argv more precisely (open from review round 1).
